title: Canning Randy
cn: 第 7 集 · 解雇兰迪
novel: Zoey [[enrolled|enroll]] in Ted's architecture class at the university. At first, Ted thought it was a [[coincidence|coincidence]], but he soon realized that Zoey had an [[ulterior|ulterior]] motive. She wanted to [[manipulate|manipulate]] his students into joining her campaign to save the Arcadian building. She asked clever questions in class and [[steered|steer]] every discussion toward the topic of historic [[preservation|preservation]]. Ted was impressed by her [[knowledge|knowledge]] but also [[suspicious|suspicious]] of her intentions. Meanwhile, Marshall and Lily went to the Halloween parade in Greenwich Village. To their shock, they [[spotted|spot]] Robin in the parade of shame. She was wearing a [[costume|costume]] and looked completely [[humiliated|humiliate]]. It turned out that Robin had been [[broadcasting|broadcast]] the parade for her news show and had accidentally become part of a [[humiliating|humiliate]] segment. Marshall tried to [[rescue|rescue]] Robin from the situation, but she told him to stay away. She did not want her friends to see her like this. Back at the university, Ted [[confronted|confront]] Zoey after class. He told her that using his students for her [[agenda|agenda]] was unacceptable. Zoey [[apologized|apologize]] and said she genuinely wanted to learn about architecture. Ted was not sure if he could [[trust|trust]] her, but he agreed to give her another chance. The episode ended with Randy, an intern at GNB, being fired by Barney for [[incompetence|incompetence]]. Randy [[begged|beg]] for his job, and Barney [[reluctantly|reluctant]] gave him one last chance. It was a day full of [[awkward|awkward]] encounters and second chances.

enroll.en: to officially join a school or class

coincidence.en: when two things happen at the same time by chance

manipulate.en: to control someone cleverly for your own purpose

steer.en: to guide the direction of something

preservation.en: the act of keeping something safe

knowledge.en: information and understanding you have learned

suspicious.en: feeling that something is not right

spot.en: to see or notice something suddenly

costume.en: clothes worn to look like someone else

humiliate.en: to make someone feel ashamed in public

broadcast.en: to send out a program on television or radio

rescue.en: to save someone from a dangerous situation

confront.en: to speak to someone directly about a problem

agenda.en: a plan or list of things to do

apologize.en: to say sorry for something wrong

trust.en: to believe someone is honest and reliable

incompetence.en: the lack of skill to do a job well
